title: Metabolic Workup in One Draw
code: PES 2015 · GalNet 2017 · US/Canada 2017 · NPC consensus 2018 · HLH-2004

blocks.text: **Never delay glucose, antibiotics, IV acyclovir, vitamin K or stopping lactose to get a sample.** Draw the extra tubes in the same stick when it costs no time. If it costs time, treat now and use the fallbacks below.

sub: Send: critical sample — glucose, bicarbonate, beta-hydroxybutyrate, lactate, insulin and C-peptide; extra plasma held.
Why: treatment changes beta-hydroxybutyrate, free fatty acids and insulin quickly (PES 2015).
Send: urine reducing substances.
Why: they turn negative off lactose; a negative result then means nothing.
Send: red-cell GALT — donor cells carry the enzyme, so the result is falsely normal.
Send: plasma 7-DHC if Smith–Lemli–Opitz syndrome is possible — cholesterol-rich feeds or blood confuse the sterols (lesson 02-11).
Send: dried-blood-spot LAL and ASM activity if the spleen is big — may be confounded (expert opinion).

items.t: Before the first dose of UDCA
sub: Send: urine bile acids by mass spectrometry.
Why: UDCA metabolites obscure the profile (NASPGHAN/ESPGHAN 2017, tier 2).

items.t: Before IV dextrose and protein restriction
sub: Send: ammonia, plasma amino acids, acylcarnitine profile, urine organic acids and orotic acid (Savy 2018).
Why: the pattern is clearest in the crisis (expert opinion).

items.t: Before parenteral vitamin K or plasma
sub: Send: INR, factors V, VII, VIII and fibrinogen.
Why: the pre-dose values are the baseline (see Prolonged INR).

blocks.h: One draw: sick infant with cholestasis, liver failure or low glucose

groups.label: Bedside — now
items: Ammonia — free-flowing, no tourniquet, on ice, to the lab at once

groups.label: Blood — same stick
items: Newborn screen result — and whether the program measures succinylacetone

groups.label: Urine — first void
items: Reducing substances — while still on lactose
Bile acids by mass spectrometry — before UDCA

groups.label: If glucose is low — critical sample
items: Beta-hydroxybutyrate and bicarbonate with the glucose
Insulin and C-peptide — hyperinsulinism also causes low glucose with cholestasis
Extra plasma held for free fatty acids and carnitine

groups.label: If the spleen is big
items: NPC bile acid marker or lyso-SM-509

sub: A tourniquet, a squeezed heel or a slow trip to the lab raises it.
Free-flowing sample on ice; stable < 15 min at 4 °C; no capillary sample (Savy 2018).
Repeat a high value — but never delay treatment of a symptomatic child.
Negative once lactose stops.
Red-cell GALT is the diagnostic test (GalNet 2017).
Many infants with tyrosinemia type 1 have normal tyrosine before 48 h; tyrosine-first screening may miss about 28% (Chinsky 2017).
Coagulopathy out of proportion to jaundice → send succinylacetone, whatever the newborn screen said.
High in every newborn; judge it against age and follow the trend.
Very high AFP with high citrulline and high GGT → citrin deficiency (NICCD).
≥ 500 µg/L is one HLH-2004 criterion (Henter 2007).
Above 10,000 µg/L was 90% sensitive and 96% specific for HLH in a mixed pediatric series (Allen 2008).
High in GALD too — ferritin does not separate GALD from HLH.
Low GGT with high bile acids and itch → transport defect (PFIC).
Low GGT with low or normal bile acids and no itch → synthesis defect.
A tendency, not a rule.
Also appear in severe liver disease of any cause and in the first weeks of life.
Repeat the urine and sequence AKR1D1 before calling it 5β-reductase deficiency.
Spuriously high in neonatal cholestasis.
Use the plasma bile acid marker or lyso-SM-509 (Geberhiwot 2018).
Urine galactitol and GALT genotype; keep the infant galactose-free until settled (GeneReviews 2021).
Stop it for 7–10 days, then send urine bile acids (lesson 02-07).

items.t: Glucose given before the critical sample
sub: Do not fast a sick infant to repeat it.
Endocrinology and metabolic teams plan a supervised fast later (PES 2015).
A gene panel that includes LIPA, SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2.

blocks.h: Feed and treat while results run

sub: Galactose-free formula at once — soy-based, casein hydrolysate or elemental — before confirmation (GalNet 2017).

items.t: Sick after sucrose, fructose or sorbitol
sub: Hereditary fructose intolerance possible: read the formula label; use a sucrose-free formula.
Diagnose by ALDOB sequencing — never by fructose challenge.
Start nitisinone with the metabolic team; do not wait for the gene (Chinsky 2017).
Treat hypoglycemia with IV glucose as usual; avoid persistent hyperglycemia.
Never give glycerol- or fructose-containing osmotic infusions (Hayasaka 2024).
Lactose-free, MCT-rich formula; involve the metabolic team.

items.text: The sample that matters is taken before the first treatment; everything after is a fallback.
Splenomegaly in a cholestatic infant adds ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble CD25 and enzyme activities to the same draw (NASPGHAN/ESPGHAN 2017).
Citrin deficiency: a 10% dextrose bolus for low glucose is safe; avoid prolonged hyperglycemia, glycerol and fructose (Hayasaka 2024).
A normal newborn screen from a tyrosine-only program does not exclude tyrosinemia type 1.
Transfused before GALT was sent: the normal GALT is the donor's.
Hypoglycemia with cholestasis called hypopituitarism without an insulin level: hyperinsulinism (for example, Kabuki syndrome) is missed.
A high ammonia from a capillary or delayed sample: repeat it properly, while treating the child in front of you.

positions.naspghan_espghan_2017_nc: Urine reducing substances tier 1; red-cell GALT tier 2 (per lesson 02-06)
positions.welling_2017_galnet: Red-cell GALT, with genotype; galactose-free diet on suspicion

rows.note: Reducing substances fail once lactose stops; GALT is the test that decides.

positions.chinsky_2017_ht1: Succinylacetone as the primary marker; tyrosine alone may miss about 28%

rows.note: No ESPGHAN or EASL statement (lesson 02-06). A normal tyrosine-based screen is false reassurance.

rows.topic: Niemann–Pick C test in a cholestatic infant

positions.naspghan_espghan_2017_nc: NPC1 among the causes; no biomarker advice (per lesson 02-10)
positions.geberhiwot_2018_npc: Plasma bile acid marker preferred; oxysterols spurious in neonatal cholestasis

rows.note: Geberhiwot 2018: order the bile acid marker or lyso-SM-509, not oxysterols.

positions.naspghan_espghan_2017_nc: Splenomegaly points to storage or hematologic disease; HLH not named (per lesson 02-10)
positions.henter_2007_hlh2004: Five of eight criteria, or a molecular diagnosis

rows.note: Add ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen and soluble CD25 when the spleen is big.
